quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Lean when the operator leans.
Hold onto their seat.
Sit as far back on the bike as possible.
Never hold onto the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when the operator leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean the same way they do. Sit as close to the operator as you can without crowding them. Hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What should you do if you must ride over an obstacle?

options.text: Slow down as much as you can.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up if possible.
Stay on your seat and lift your feet off the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as you can.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and hit it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep your motorcycle straight. Just before hitting it, ease off the throttle slightly to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: What should you focus on when adjusting your mirrors?

options.text: The road behind and beside your motorcycle.
Your arms.
The road in front of your motorcycle.
The side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and beside your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much of the lane beside you as possible. A mirror may show part of your arm or shoulder, but what matters most is seeing the road behind and beside you.

questions.question: Where do motorcycle operators and other drivers have the most conflicts?

options.text: At intersections
On highways
On rural roads
In parking lots

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections have the highest risk of conflicts between motorcycle riders and other drivers. Riders should be extra careful when entering and riding through intersections.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for your friend.
Distract your friend with other activities.
Keep your friend from leaving until they are sober.
Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: There are several ways to stop someone from riding their motorcycle while impaired. You can arrange another ride home, keep them busy with other activities to slow their drinking, stop them from leaving before they are sober, and ask other friends to help intervene together.

questions.question: How should you brake?

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam the front brake and grab the rear brake.
Press the front brake and jam the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: To brake, squeeze the front brake lever and press down on the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
By the left foot peg
By the right foot peg

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: What protects your eyes from the wind?

options.text: Goggles
Windshield
Sunglasses
Eyeglasses

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from the wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: What percentage of motorcycle and car crashes are caused by drivers failing to yield the right-of-way?

options.text: About 10 percent
About 25 percent
Over 50 percent
About 90 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: Over 50 percent
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle and car crashes happen because drivers fail to properly yield the right-of-way to motorcycle riders.

questions.question: What should riders do in general?

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change lane positions often to avoid boredom.
Choose a lane position that gives you the most space.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives you the most space.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly, so the safest lane position also changes. Choose the position that gives you the most space and helps other drivers see you better.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Brake gradually.
Speed up.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. This will make it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed by closing the throttle. Lean forward and down, and pull off the road as soon as possible. Do not use the brakes, as they can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. Is this area safe for motorcyclists?

options.text: Never safe.
Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny.
Always safe, no matter the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil drips from cars collect in the center of the lane. When the road is dry, this area has enough grip for motorcycles. The oily strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can ride around it and still stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce the chance of an accident?

options.text: Ride only in the afternoon.
Follow the vehicle ahead as closely as possible.
Look only at your controls and not ahead.
Signal your intentions to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Stay safe by making sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show what you are doing. Keep space around your motorcycle. Watch the road ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Signs that show road rules, like speed limits, are rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow all rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, which brakes should you use?

options.text: Both front and rear brakes.
Only the rear brake to save the front brake for emergencies.
Only the front brake to save the rear brake for emergencies.
Squeeze only the front brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. This habit will help you in an emergency stop. If you practice using both brakes for normal stops, it will be easier to do in a quick stop.

questions.question: What is true about approved helmets?

options.text: They limit what you can see.
They let you see as far to the sides as you need.
They are dangerous to wear.
You do not have to wear one if you think it blocks your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: They let you see as far to the sides as you need.
questions.explanation: Some riders worry that helmets block their side vision. This is not true. An approved helmet allows you to see all the way to the sides that you need for safe riding.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Increase throttle.
Hold the handlebars loosely.
Gently brake using the tire that is not flat.
Speed up to get off the road faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake using the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat while riding, ease off the throttle and go straight as you slow down. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake of the tire that is not flat, if you know which one that is.

questions.question: After drinking alcohol, what reduces its effects?

options.text: Exercise.
Coffee.
Time.
Food.

questions.correctAnswerText: Time.
questions.explanation: Your liver breaks down alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up. The only way to reduce alcohol's effects is to wait for your body to process it.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, what should you do?

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Brake harder than usual to stop quickly.
Brake gently to avoid overworking the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: The extra weight of a passenger in a sidecar changes how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will need more distance to stop completely.

questions.question: When are motorcyclists safest?

options.text: When other motorists can see them.
When they are faster than other vehicles.
When they are on the side of the road.
When they are on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When other motorists can see them.
questions.explanation: Safe riders know they are safest when other drivers can clearly see them. Use your headlight, brake light, turn signals, and lane position to be as visible as possible.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Makes you easier to see.
Is not allowed.
Should only be used at night.
Does not help you be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you easier to see.
questions.explanation: Reflective material on a vest or helmet makes other drivers see you. Use it during the day and at night.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery road, what should you do?

options.text: Lean into the slippery section to stay balanced.
Keep your speed to improve traction.
Do not worry about the road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery roads when possible. If you cannot avoid one, keep your motorcycle straight and go as slowly as you can.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the wobble.
Use the brakes slowly.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
Shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up when your motorcycle wobbles. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slowly close the throttle to slow down, and lean forward. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: The body eliminates one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?

options.text: One drink
Two drinks
Three drinks
Four drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: Four drinks
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals about four drinks remaining.

questions.question: When riding at night, a motorcycle operator should do everything except:

options.text: Ride more slowly.
Keep more distance from other vehicles.
Use high beams whenever possible.
Follow vehicles too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow vehicles too closely.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, slow down and increase the distance between you and other vehicles. Use headlights to see ahead. Never follow other vehicles too closely.
